newsitem.title: USA: Duke says 379,800 without power after Fran.
newsitem.headline: Duke says 379,800 without power after Fran.

text.p: Duke Power Co said Friday Hurricane Fran knocked out electricity to about 379,800 of its 1.8 million customers, mostly in the northern and eastern parts of its central Carolinas service territory.
"As of 0600 EDT this morning, we had 379,800 customers without power," said company spokesman Rick Zuercher.
"We're still assessing damage. We have no information on transmission lines, but the whole region is pretty messed up," he said.
One of the hardest hit areas served by Duke was Greensboro, N.C., where 120,000 customers are lacking power.
Winston-Salem, Burlington and Durham, N.C., also caught the fury of the storm, which passed over the area late Thursday after making landfall at Cape Fear, on North Carolina's southernmost coast.
Fran slammed into the coast with winds of up to 120 mph.
Duke, based in Charlotte, N.C., said crews from unaffected areas were being moved to the hardest hit areas. At the same time, the company is seeking emergency assistance from other utilities.
As already reported by other power companies, downed trees and flooded roads are slowing damage assessment and efforts to restore power to much of the area.
Carolina Power & Light Co was the utility clobbered hardest by Fran, with service to some 670,000 of its customers disrupted.
Fran, now downgraded to a tropical storm, is moving north-northwest across neighboring Virginia, where extensive power outages also were reported this morning.

The storm, still dumping heavy rains and buffeting the region with strong winds, so far has left at least 1.5 million utility customers - or four million residents - across the southeastern U.S. without electricity.
-- J Jelter, New York Power Desk + 1 212 859 1621
